what: Round 1510. The domestic super cups Club Manager follows and plays: per country and format year (the year uclSeasonYear reads: 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020 or 2026) the cup's plain name, its shape, how a level match is settled, who gets in and who takes a place a club holds twice, where it sits in the season and whose ground it is played on; and per season one edition the clubs the real season before gave it and, for that edition only, its ground. Held as DATA with the pages it was read from. src/data/cmOneOffRows.ts states these values and scripts/simOneOffCups.mjs section 0 fails if the two disagree.
rules: A verified fact stands on two families on two hosts, none a wiki: an official one (the federation, the league, UEFA, a club) and a press one. A source that only repeats another's text counts once.
A literal is a line the page reader or the search engine quoted from the page on the read day, kept short. A date is the page's own; otherwise the source says undated.

A row that is not verified (toVerify) carries no constant: its usedBy list is empty, its id is in CM_ONE_OFF_PARTIAL, and the game plays no super cup for that country and year. Candidates written beside it are memory or another lane's notes, never facts.
A ground's name is a fact of one edition: it is printed only for the season one edition its row sources, never projected onto a later season.
The game's dates are its own: no real date and no real result is ever shown. The real 2026 result is not recorded here on purpose.

shape.note: One match, settled on the night: an annual match between the champions and the cup winners.

decider.note: Level after 90 minutes goes straight to penalties, no extra time. The official line is Arsenal FC's preview of the 2026 edition (undated; it says 2026/27 gets underway on Sunday in Cardiff); the press line is the 2026 edition's; Liverpool FC's page says the same of the 2025 edition.

entry.note: The Premier League champions against the FA Cup winners.

double.note: A club that wins both: the league runners-up take the cup's place.

place.note: Before the league season: the curtain raiser. The game plays it on the Wednesday before its own opening Saturday.

venue.note: A neutral ground, neither club's: Wembley since 1974 and Cardiff in 2026. No permanent ground is inferred: the name is printed for the season one edition only.

clubs.note: Arsenal, the 2025-26 Premier League champions (CM_FINAL_TABLES_2025_26), against Manchester City, the 2026 FA Cup winners (Round 1509's row K1, SEASON_ONE_CUP_WINNERS.premier).
